additional_concerns: All nine required pairs are retained. Their NOT_APPLICABLE assessments are limited to these claim-question relationships; they neither establish overall candidate correctness nor authorize deleting the supported claims.

The web-form claim's missing-footnote uncertainty is stale. Footnote 3 is supplied in da12aecad4e68.u30.3569: "Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission." The markers appear on XML and PDF, not the web form. Neither a web-form e-Cert requirement nor a general exemption from authentication should be invented.

node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 uses "[the fact filing_date] is greater than or equal to [date value 2026-02-02]", which includes pre-9:00am filings that day. The source separately gives a date-based channel rule, a 9:00am launch and resubmission "following its implementation". The calendar-date and operational-launch readings are not executable equivalents; retain the interpretive difference.

The instant-based candidates select an inclusive 9:00am threshold. The source gives the launch time but does not expressly state its timezone or resolve the exact-boundary interpretation of "following its implementation". Authoritative clarification is missing for resolving those issues; no supplied dependency ID can reliably be assigned to it.

The blackout passage authorizes direct contact for urgent submissions. Contact alone does not establish an actual STR filing, but the passage also does not establish that contact can never result in a filing. Keep contact, actual submission and automatic migration distinct, without treating the blackout contact arrangement as a general post-launch channel permission.

node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb puts "the fact submitted_to_jfiu" in its result, while the other event candidates put actual filing in scope. For a known non-filing by an in-scope firm, this can produce FALSE versus OUT_OF_SCOPE. Whether that difference matters depends on whether non-filings are admissible inputs to the typed original-submission-event question.

node.fc565a946804e1633024b4d3 delegates historical existence and sufficient-history assessment to a supplied Boolean. Its executable does not quantify over events or establish history completeness. A negative result requires the stipulated evidence sufficient to rule out a triggering event; absence of a recorded event alone is insufficient.

The history candidate scopes the responsible entity, whereas node.8caddb7a4c29338c1d340db1 scopes the original submitter. Their equivalence is not established for agent submissions, changes in responsibility or changes in licensed status. The source's reference to licensed firms does not itself resolve every event-to-entity relationship.

The typed DUTY_TRIGGER questions make TRUE denote trigger occurrence, despite the general label TRUE_IS_SATISFIED. A later STREAMS 2 resubmission does not erase the original triggering event. These formulas do not determine whether the resulting duty remains outstanding or has been discharged.

Neither web-form permission nor XML technical-test liaison is an additional prerequisite to the quoted resubmission trigger. Requiring either would add an unsupported restriction. Conversely, absence of a resubmission trigger does not grant permission to use another channel.

The separate JFIU XML schema and promised resubmission guidance are referenced but their contents are not supplied. The catalogue contains only opaque dependency IDs with null source_hash values, so no AVAILABLE assessment or reliable document-to-ID mapping is possible. These missing documents do not prevent establishing the narrow permission and liaison claims assessed here.
